name: Topicary REST API
description:
The Topicary REST API lets you manage a single project's content
programmatically: create and edit topics and reusable components, organize
maps, inspect publication targets, and register webhooks.

## Base URL

```
https://topicary.com/api/v1
```

## Authentication

Every request must include an API key as a bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer tk_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Generate keys in **Project Settings → API Keys**. A key is scoped to the
project it was created in and inherits that project's plan. The plaintext
key is shown only once at creation; Topicary stores only a SHA-256 hash.

## Response envelope

Authoring endpoints use `data` on success, `error` on failure,
and a `meta` block on list endpoints:

```
Success (one)    { "data": { ... } }
Success (list)   { "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "total", "offset", "limit" } }
Error (4xx/5xx)  { "error": "message" }
DELETE           204 No Content (empty body)
```

`GET /targets/{targetId}/pages` returns its published-page DTO directly:
`{ "generationId", "pages", "nextCursor", "site"? }`, with no `data` or
`meta` wrapper. Failures use `error` and an optional machine-readable `code`.

## Pagination

Authoring list endpoints accept `offset` (default `0`) and `limit` (default `50`,
maximum `100`) query parameters and report `meta.total` for the full count.
Published pages instead use an opaque, generation-bound `cursor` and
`nextCursor`; restart from the first page if the served generation changes.

## Rate limits

Authoring requests are limited to **1000 requests per minute per API
key**. Unauthenticated requests (bad or missing keys) are limited to 100
per minute per IP. Published pages have a separate **300 requests per minute
per validated API key** limit. Exceeding a limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`.

## Request bodies

Send `Content-Type: application/json`. JSON request bodies are capped at
**1 MB** by default; topic creation and updates allow **3 MiB**. Document content is TipTap/ProseMirror JSON — a `content_json`
object with `type: "doc"` and a `content` array.
